E1.evidence:
Issue ros/geometry2#84 (bricerebsamen, 2015-03-11): "after #74 I get this error
/opt/ros/indigo/lib/libtf.so: undefined reference to `tf2::BufferCore::_allFramesAsDot() const'

to reproduce: create a workspace with the ros/velodyne repo and the ros/geometry_experimental repo, both of them checked out to the latest version.

I bisected on ros/geometry_experimental and I confirmed #74 is the culprit". Maintainer tfoote reworked the change ("I've also attempted a rework to overload instead of have a default method. Can you try the fix_84 branch?", "I patched fix_84 for _allFramesAsDOT as well.") and the reporter confirmed "yep that fixes it!"; PR #86 'Use overloading instead of default arguments' ('Fixes #84') was merged as 04810475 on 2015-03-12.

E2.evidence: Step 1: tf (package tf in ros/geometry; the indigo binary /opt/ros/indigo/lib/libtf.so, whose tf::Transformer::allFramesAsDot is `return tf2_buffer_._allFramesAsDot();`) and tf2 (package tf2 in ros/geometry2; libtf2.so and tf2/buffer_core.h, built from the reporter's source overlay). Separately released packages from different repositories. Step 2: the failing value is the symbol the consumer references across the library boundary: libtf.so needs `tf2::BufferCore::_allFramesAsDot() const` and the overlay's tf2 no longer exports it; with the provider at its earlier declaration the same consumer links, so it is an interface failure. Step 3: no names rebound. Step 4: the resolution is a source change to the provider's declarations (overloads instead of a default argument), not a build-system change, although the trigger was a binary consumer mixed with a source-overlay provider (tfoote: "You shouldn't be using symbols from /opt/ros that depend on a source overlay."). Step 5: no firmware. Step 6: eligible; library API (C++ ABI of tf2::BufferCore).

E3.evidence: UPGRADE: the provider (tf2, source overlay at the indigo-devel head of 2015-03-11, which contains PR #74) runs at a newer revision than the one the binary consumer (tf 1.11.4 deb) was built against (tf2 0.5.7); the consumer still references `_allFramesAsDot()` as declared at that earlier revision. No other operation is supported.

E4.evidence: Observed failure: link error "/opt/ros/indigo/lib/libtf.so: undefined reference to `tf2::BufferCore::_allFramesAsDot() const'" reported by the reporter, bisected to #74.

units.name: tf2
units.revision_basis: The reporter built ros/geometry_experimental (now ros/geometry2) 'checked out to the latest version' on 2015-03-11T19:11Z; the indigo-devel head at that time was 2fd8395d (2015-03-03T09:03:23Z, merge of #76), which contains PR #74 'change _allFramesAsDot() -> _allFramesAsDot(double current_time)' merged as cbcc785c on 2015-03-03T08:59:34Z (GitHub's merge_commit_sha 4bfd657e for #74 does not exist in the repository). At 2fd8395d tf2/include/tf2/buffer_core.h declares `std::string _allFramesAsDot(double current_time = 0) const;` and `std::string allFramesAsYAML(double current_time = 0) const;`. The reporter bisected the regression to #74. The resolved revision is the merge of PR #86 (fix_84) on indigo-devel, 2015-03-12T01:53:32Z; the reporter verified the fix_84 branch head de715513 ('fix DOT as well'), whose tf2/include/tf2/buffer_core.h (blob c2ea7c2e) and tf2/src/buffer_core.cpp (blob 4fa055ef) are identical to those at 04810475. Both #74 and #86 were first released together in tf2 0.5.8 (2015-03-17).

units.name: tf
units.revision_basis: The consumer is the indigo binary /opt/ros/indigo/lib/libtf.so, pulled into the link of a velodyne target in the reporter's workspace ('So tf is pulled from `/opt/ros/indigo`'); per tf/CHANGELOG.rst, 1.11.4 (2014-12-23) was the geometry indigo release current on 2015-03-11 (1.11.5 followed on 2015-03-17). At 1.11.4 tf/src/tf.cpp contains `std::string Transformer::allFramesAsDot() const { return tf2_buffer_._allFramesAsDot(); }`. The resolution does not change tf.

loudness_evidence: The linker reports "undefined reference to `tf2::BufferCore::_allFramesAsDot() const'" while building the reporter's workspace (catkin_tools); tfoote's reproduction shows the same class of error for tf2_ros: "/tmp/catkin_workspace/devel_isolated/tf2_ros/lib/libtf2_ros.so: undefined reference to `tf2::BufferCore::allFramesAsYAML() const'\ncollect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status".

resolution.summary: Use overloading instead of default arguments (PR #86): tf2::BufferCore declares `std::string _allFramesAsDot(double current_time) const;` plus `std::string _allFramesAsDot() const;` implemented as `return _allFramesAsDot(0.0);`, and likewise `allFramesAsYAML(double current_time) const` plus `allFramesAsYAML() const` ("Backwards compatibility for #84"), so the zero-argument symbols referenced by consumers built against the earlier declaration are exported again. The consumer is unchanged.
resolution.evidence: Reporter bricerebsamen, 2015-03-12T01:23:13Z: "yep that fixes it!" after tfoote's "I patched fix_84 for _allFramesAsDOT as well." (fix_84 head de715513, tf2 files identical to the merge 04810475), with the unchanged indigo binary libtf.so (tf 1.11.4).

notes: Two entries describe one declaration change from two sides: at source level the declaration was retyped (a defaulted parameter added), and at the binary level the zero-argument symbol the consumer's compiled code references (default arguments are expanded in the caller) is no longer exported, which is what the linker reports. consumer_built_against is inferred: libtf.so's reference matches the declaration `std::string _allFramesAsDot() const;` at tf2 0.5.7 (2014-12-23, released the same day as tf 1.11.4 and current until 0.5.8 on 2015-03-17). The reporter's third unit, ros/velodyne, is the workspace package whose executable link pulled in libtf.so; it is not a party to the failed interface. tfoote's allFramesAsYAML observations concern tf2_ros inside the same overlay linking against stale devel/install artifacts of tf2 ("First pass is producing a void argument symbol, rming devel and build produces double"), a different composition (tf2_ros <-> tf2) that PR #86 also covers; not a condition of this case. Binary users were never exposed because 0.5.8 shipped #74 and #86 together. Dataset codes: EVOLUTION:LIBRARY, SOFTWARE:BUILD.
